brief_rationale: The doctor maintained a safe responsibility chain throughout: they avoided unsupported diagnosis or medication changes, recognized the recent stent/dual antiplatelet and pure red cell aplasia risks, and repeatedly converted uncertainty into named questions for thoracic surgery, cardiology, hematology, anesthesia, nurses, and records/pharmacy channels. Closure was safe and bounded, with discharge medication execution, 1-week thoracic follow-up, hematology blood-count follow-up, and urgent escalation thresholds. Multiple high-order points were actively completed, especially repairing the perioperative responsibility chain and navigating fragmented records/poor access, so the deterministic grade is Perfect.

closure_assessment.explanation: The episode was safely bounded at discharge/home transition: medication use was tied to the circled discharge instructions, thoracic surgery review was to be arranged within 1 week, blood-count follow-up was assigned to hematology, and red flags required ED/120. Some uncertainties remained, especially exact blood values and final surgical pathway, but they were explicitly carried forward with owners and safety thresholds.
